title: Functional-Redundancy vs Response-Diversity: An Ecosystem-Function Lens on Safe Failure

original_idea.body:
# Functional-Redundancy vs Response-Diversity

Adapt ecology's response-diversity vs functional-redundancy framework; on safety tasks separate surface variation (wording) from functional variation (decisions/error patterns) across a model panel to show how much apparent diversity is merely stylistic. Inference + decomposition.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 3: plausible chain (separating cosmetic vs functional diversity warns against false comfort) but the catastrophic link is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 4: 2-level decomposition separating surface vs functional variation; operationalizing functional adds complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 4: focused deliverable (surface vs functional split) but operationalizing functional variation is a dependency.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 4: public models + conceptual framework, no internal access, weak lab incentive.

novelty.reasoning: Applying the ecology functional-redundancy lens to LLM safety appears largely novel.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: No known application of functional-redundancy vs response-diversity to LLM safety.
